reasons: Covers the main failure paths by running the real script, which is good evidence.
The test named for a missing file writes an empty file instead, so true absence is not tested here.
Needs real generated results present, so it cannot run on a fresh checkout without a replay first.

terms.meaning: the tool that finds and runs test files and reports pass or fail
a separate program started by another program, used here to run the collector
a saved sample of data used in place of real input
the number a program returns to show success (0) or failure (1)
the program that runs JavaScript outside a browser

depends_on: Node.js built-in modules node:child_process, node:fs, node:os and node:path
evals/results/value.json, evals/results/manifest.json, evals/results/portfolio.json and one candidate record
used_by: Run by the frontend test command; no caller is visible in the packet.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and the reason for it
sections.what: Imports the test tools and file helpers, and sets the paths to the collector and the repository root. The header explains that these tests run the script rather than inspect its text.
sections.why: The header says an earlier check that searched the source text would have passed even if the logic had been deleted.
sections.watch_out: The repository root is calculated from this file's location, so moving the file breaks every path in the tests.

sections.name: fixtureRoot
sections.title: Building a test copy of the repository
sections.what: Creates a temporary folder with copies of the real result files, one candidate record and one golden case under a made-up industry name, then applies any change the test asks for.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test can break one file in its own copy without touching the real repository.
sections.watch_out: The copy is made from real files at test time, so regenerating those files can change what the tests exercise.

sections.name: run
sections.title: Running the collector as a separate program
sections.what: Starts the collector as a separate program pointed at a given folder with an output file inside it, then reports the exit code, the error text, and whether a bundle was written.
sections.why: Likely reason: running the script the same way a developer would means the tests check the real exit code and error text.
sections.watch_out: The output file sits inside the test folder, so a bundle written during a test never touches the real generated file.

sections.name: a complete tree
sections.title: Complete tree produces a bundle
sections.what: Checks that with nothing broken, the collector exits successfully and writes a bundle.
sections.why: Reason stated in the test: it is the baseline, so that a failing test points at the broken copy and not at the setup.
sections.watch_out: It checks only success and that a file exists, not what the bundle contains.

sections.name: a missing artefact
sections.title: Unreadable value file stops the collector
sections.what: Replaces the value file with an empty file, then checks that the collector exits with failure, writes nothing, and names the value file in its error.
sections.why: The test name says missing, but an empty file is unreadable rather than absent, so this really tests the unreadable path.
sections.watch_out: A file deleted entirely is not tested here, so true absence needs its own test.

sections.name: a truncated artefact
sections.title: Truncated file is named, not crashed
sections.what: Cuts the manifest short so it is no longer valid JSON, then checks that the collector exits with failure, writes nothing, and names the manifest file with the word malformed.
sections.why: Reason stated in the test name: an earlier version raised a parse error that named no file.
sections.watch_out: The test depends on the exact word malformed in the collector's messages, so rewording that message breaks the test even if the behaviour is right.

sections.name: valid JSON of the wrong shape
sections.title: Wrong-shape files are refused
sections.what: Three checks: an empty object in place of the value file, a manifest with its run identifier removed, and a value file with its bridges list emptied. Each must exit with failure and name the problem.
sections.why: The comments say the empty object case once passed every check and crashed the viewer, so it is the main regression guard here.
sections.watch_out: The checks look for fixed phrases such as missing required key and empty array, so rewording those messages breaks the tests.

sections.name: no candidate records
sections.title: No candidate records stops the collector
sections.what: Builds a folder with no candidate records and checks that the collector exits with failure and names the candidates folder pattern.
sections.why: Reason stated in the test: the collector should stop rather than render an empty portfolio.
sections.watch_out: The test does not check that no bundle was written, even though its name implies it stops without output.

summary: Runs the collector script on copies of the real result files, breaking one thing at a time, to confirm that each failure path stops the script and names the problem.
purpose: Checks that the collector refuses bad input rather than writing a bundle that looks like real data.
why: The header says an earlier version of this test only checked the script's text, so it would have passed with all its logic deleted. These tests run the script instead.
how: Builds a temporary folder by copying the real value, manifest and portfolio files, one candidate record and one golden case. For each test it changes or removes one file, runs the collector as a separate program, and checks the exit code, whether a bundle was written, and the error text.
inputs: The real result files under the results folder and one golden case input, read from the repository. Temporary folders are created for each test.
outputs: Pass or fail results from the test runner. The repository itself is not changed, but temporary folders are left behind in the system temp area.
risks: The tests depend on real result files existing, so on a fresh checkout they fail during setup. The test named for a missing artefact actually writes an empty file, so it checks the unreadable path rather than true absence. Temporary folders are never removed.
debug: If every test fails during setup, run the replay first so the real result files exist. If one test fails, read its assertion and the matching group in this file. Remember that the missing-artefact test writes an empty file. Run the test runner on this file alone to isolate the failure.
